title: 2025 capital budget and 10-year forecast review
subtitle: Debt, development charges, reserves, budget communication, parks, traffic calming and the $1M one-time strategic funding discussed.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee spent the afternoon reviewing the 2025 Capital Budget and 10-Year Forecast. Its only motion was to receive the report for information {{vote:m1}}. Because the committee did not amend the forecast, the proposed capital plan goes forward unchanged for the Mayor's budget proposal and Council's final budget decisions.

Staff explained that more than half of capital funding comes from self-funded enterprises such as water, sanitary and stormwater utilities, with development charges and the capital pool next. The City's debt has been falling, though growth-related debt backed by development charges is rising. Staff said a large shortfall remains, especially for facilities, and that provincial and federal funding is needed.

Councillors also discussed a proposed radio and digital campaign to explain the City's share of the tax bill, how reliable road reconstruction timelines are, parkland acquisition, and a $1M one-time strategic funding option. Staff agreed to follow up on several items, including reporting to ward councillors on project timing, reserve interest, and the use of heritage and brownfield programs.

decisions.detail: The committee received the 2025 Capital Budget and 10-Year Forecast (report FIN-2024-513) for information, with no changes to the proposed forecast.

debate: Councillors pressed staff on road reconstruction timelines. Staff said the first budget year is usually design, that work must be coordinated with the Region and utilities, and that the forecast now covers five years rather than ten. Staff agreed to update ward councillors periodically.

On communications, councillors wanted residents to understand that the City's share is about 30% of the tax bill. They suggested using community centre signage, bolder bill inserts and neighbourhood association social media. Staff proposed a 2025 radio and geo-targeted digital campaign.

On development charges, councillors asked about deferrals and infill. Staff said deferrals create cash-flow pressure, and rental housing already gets a five-year deferral. They also said a full study would be needed to change how charges are set, with the next one planned for 2027.

Some councillors raised parkland needs and asked whether acquisition could be funded now. Staff said the recreational land reserve is restricted to that purpose, targeted purchases would come as separate reports, and a broader strategy is due in 2025.

Councillors asked for more funding for small-scale traffic calming such as flexible posts. Staff said the program runs a small annual deficit and offered to report back on how earlier added funding was used.
